title: Your morning
hookLine: design a morning practice you can keep for years
tomorrow: Mai's roommate is a total stranger. so where does she sit?

cards: For some of us the morning starts with a thumb on the phone before the eyes are open. Mai's mornings this summer start with a 7am studio call, six weeks of them. Can a morning practice survive that?

It can, if it's small enough. The Buddha's mornings, as the suttas tell them, weren't long. Sutta after sutta opens the same way: in the morning he dressed, took his bowl and robe, and walked into town for alms.

teach.h: THE SAME FEW ACTS, IN ORDER.
teach.b: That stock opening is the first thing to notice. The same few acts, in the same order: dress, bowl, walk. A morning kept for years isn't heroic.
It's a small shape, repeated until it holds you. The suttas also give mornings a picture.

teach.h: THE DAWN: FORERUNNER OF THE SUN.
teach.b: In one short sutta the dawn is called the forerunner of the sunrise, the first sign that the sun is coming, and the Buddha uses it for what comes before the path. A morning practice works like that dawn.
It doesn't finish the day; it tells the day what kind of day it is. Buddhist mornings carry this in the senses.

teach.h: A BELL, A BOW, A CUP OF WATER.
teach.b: In temples a bell sounds before morning chanting. Theravada monks in parts of Asia still walk the alms round in early light, and families wait at the roadside with rice.
At home it can be a cup of water set on the altar, a stick of incense, one bow. Ông's morning, for years, has been watering his bonsai before anything else. None of it takes long.
What makes it practice is that it comes first, and it comes back tomorrow.
So build yours for the worst morning, not the best: the bad sleep, the early call.
Small enough to keep for years.

how: Buddhist mornings take many forms: morning chanting after a bell in temples, the alms round in Theravada countries, and at home a bow, water or incense at a small altar, and a short sit before the day begins.

the first small acts of your day, kept in the same order
a long meditation you have to finish before sunrise

games.q: your cousin starts a new job and wants a morning practice. her plan: a full hour of meditation at 5am, starting monday. what fits today's teaching?
o: start with a few minutes she can keep on her worst morning, same order daily
go for the full hour; a big start builds the habit faster
wait until the job settles down, then design something bigger
games.why: the sutta mornings are small acts repeated: dress, bowl, walk. a practice kept for years is sized for the worst morning.

practice: Sit up with both feet flat on the floor. Rub your palms together until they're warm, rest them over your closed eyes, then lower your hands and open your eyes to whatever light is in the room.
Stay with that first light, as if it were dawn, for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: Your morning: the first small acts of the day, in the same order, the dawn before the day itself.

orig.note: Pali: the dawn, the red light before sunrise. In the sutta it's the forerunner of the sun.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: a morning, for years, small enough for the worst day. Day done.

sources.ref: the suttas' stock morning, e.g. Digha Nikaya 2 and many sutta openings: 'in the morning he dressed, took bowl and robe, and entered for alms'
